name: Street Custom 'Brimstone' Thermite Grenade
description: An improvised thermite incendiary device constructed from commercially available iron oxide and aluminum powder packed into a metal container with a magnesium ribbon fuse. The Brimstone burns at approximately 2,500°C for 10-15 seconds, producing molten iron that will burn through virtually any material it contacts — steel plate, engine blocks, vault doors, and human tissue with equal indifference. The device cannot be extinguished once ignited and produces intense white light and acrid smoke. The components are available from industrial supply outlets without restriction, and the assembly requires no specialized knowledge — recipes circulate freely through Tier 1 fabrication networks.
specifications:
burn temperature: approximately 2,500°C
burn duration: 10-15 seconds
penetration: Will burn through 15mm mild steel
ignition: Magnesium ribbon fuse, 3-second delay
weight: 0.5-1.5 kg depending on container
components: Iron oxide powder, aluminum powder, metal container
countermeasure: Cannot be extinguished — must burn out
construction time: 20 minutes with available materials
story_hooks: A series of vault breaches across Tier 2 all used Brimstone devices to melt through the doors — the thermite composition analysis shows identical chemical ratios, indicating a single supplier.
Someone is dropping Brimstone devices through storm drains into the underground tunnel networks, targeting infrastructure — the fires are unreachable by emergency services.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crudely cylindrical metal container with an aggressive, utilitarian silhouette. The device resembles a industrial thermos wrapped in danger — compact, dense, and deliberately unmarked. The magnesium ribbon fuse protrudes from the top like a lit match waiting to ignite.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 12-15 cm, Diameter: 6-8 cm, Fuse length: 4-5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively heavy for its size — substantial heft in the palm, roughly 0.5-1.5 kg depending on payload density. Feels like holding compressed potential.
physical_description.primary_material: Welded steel or aluminum alloy container, commercial-grade metal stock. Interior lined with thermite paste (iron oxide and aluminum powder mixture).
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray or bare welded steel with heat-stressed discoloration. No polish — functional and crude. Solder drips visible at seams.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with oxidized brown/rust staining near the base. Silver-gray magnesium ribbon fuse at apex. Occasional red oxide dust residue from poor sealing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare cold metal or light corrosion texture. Some versions wrapped with electrical tape or cloth strips for handling. Unpleasant to grip — industrial sharp edges, no ergonomic consideration.
distinctive_features: Exposed magnesium ribbon fuse jutting from crown with slight curl or kink
Uneven welding seams with visible spatter and surface irregularities
Rust bloom or oxidation stains suggesting age or poor storage conditions
Scoring or hash marks scratched into the metal body (user assembly marks or tally counts)
Slight dents or dings indicating rough handling and transport
Fine residual powder dust visible in crevices and around the base rim
No serial numbers, logos, or identification — deliberately anonymous
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None. Street Custom devices are unmarked by design — no corporate accountability, no traceable origin. May have crude hand-scratched initials or gang symbols from the fabricator.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-worn and weathered. These are single-use instruments, stored in suboptimal conditions — humidity-prone, roughly handled, dust-covered. Rust bloom is expected. The fuse is slightly discolored from age or exposure.
